questions.stem: What is the formula for calculating the harmonic mean of two numbers, x and y?
questions.solution: The harmonic mean of two numbers, x and y, is calculated as 2xy / (x + y). This formula ensures that the average rate (harmonic mean) is used when finding the mean of two quantities that are inversely proportional, such as distance and time.
questions.explanation: The arithmetic mean (A) is the sum divided by the count, not applicable here. The geometric mean (B) calculates the square root of the product, which is different from the harmonic mean. Option D represents multiplication, not an average.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Confusing harmonic mean with arithmetic or geometric means.

questions.stem: What is the result when a number n is harmonically divided by m?
questions.solution: Harmonic division is the inverse of multiplication. So, if you have a number n divided by m, the harmonic division would be m divided by n.
questions.explanation: Option A represents simple division, not harmonic division. Option C and D involve additional calculations that are not part of harmonic division.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Applying arithmetic operations instead of understanding the concept of harmonic division.

questions.stem: If two sets of numbers, A and B, have equal harmonic means, what can be concluded about their medians?

choices.A: The median of set A is greater than the median of set B.
choices.B: The median of set A is less than the median of set B.
choices.C: The median of set A is equal to the median of set B.
choices.D: There is not enough information to determine.

questions.solution: Knowing only the harmonic means of two sets does not provide sufficient information to compare their medians.
questions.explanation: Harmonic mean and median are different concepts, and knowing one does not directly reveal information about the other. Thus, without additional data, we cannot make any conclusions about the medians.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Assuming a direct relationship between harmonic means and medians.

questions.stem: In a sequence of numbers, if the harmonic mean equals the arithmetic mean, what can be inferred?

choices.A: All numbers in the sequence are equal.
choices.B: The sequence contains only two distinct numbers.
choices.C: The sequence has an even number of terms.
choices.D: There is not enough information to determine.

questions.solution: If the harmonic mean equals the arithmetic mean, it implies that all the numbers in the sequence are equal. This is because the harmonic mean becomes equal to the arithmetic mean only when all values are identical.
questions.explanation: In a sequence with unequal terms, the arithmetic mean will always be greater than the harmonic mean. Thus, equality can only occur if all terms are the same.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Assuming that two different types of means must always differ.

questions.stem: The harmonic mean of a set of numbers is 12. If one number in the set is doubled, what will happen to the harmonic mean?
questions.solution: When one number in a set is doubled, the harmonic mean remains unchanged because the effect of doubling one term is offset by the halving of its reciprocal in the calculation.
questions.explanation: The harmonic mean is sensitive to changes in values but not when they are multiplied or divided by the same factor. Doubling one number and halving its reciprocal keeps the harmonic mean constant.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Assuming that doubling a term will proportionally change the harmonic mean.

questions.stem: The harmonic mean of two numbers is 6. If both numbers are increased by the same positive value, what will happen to the harmonic mean?

choices.D: It may increase or decrease depending on the size of the increment.

questions.solution: When both numbers in a set are increased by the same positive value, the harmonic mean increases because the effect of increasing both terms is greater than the halving of their reciprocals.
questions.explanation: Increasing both numbers proportionally reduces their reciprocals more, leading to an overall increase in the harmonic mean.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Assuming that increasing both numbers will have no effect on the harmonic mean.

questions.stem: The harmonic mean of a set of positive integers is 10. If the largest number in the set is removed, what will happen to the harmonic mean?

choices.D: It may increase or decrease depending on the size of the largest number.

questions.solution: When the largest number in a set of positive integers is removed, the harmonic mean decreases because the remaining numbers have a greater influence on the average.
questions.explanation: Removing the largest value reduces the overall sum and increases the reciprocals of the remaining terms, leading to a decrease in the harmonic mean.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Assuming that removing any number will not affect the harmonic mean if the other numbers remain.
